4: Unit 1: what the P R V groups have to hold.
Two Microsoft features meet in a P R V group.
Microsoft Learn's page on using groups to manage role assignments says only a group created with is Assignable To Role set to true can hold an Entra role.
It's set at creation and can't be changed.
A tenant can have at most five hundred.
Membership must be assigned, never dynamic, and a group can't be a member.
The second is pim for Groups: just-in-time membership or ownership, with one policy for membership and one for ownership.
The program's design uses them together in two ways.
For an Entra role, the group holds an eligible assignment, and its members are active.
For other privilege, such as an Azure role, the members are eligible for the group.
The access packages for P R V membership, the plan's A3.3, aren't built here.
5: Three facts from Microsoft Learn's pim for Groups pages shape the code.
First, eligible membership doesn't appear in the group's members list, so reading members alone would miss every eligible holder.
Second, pim onboards a group on its first schedule or policy change, and the group can't be taken back out; the policy I D's change when that happens.
Third, group administrators or owners can override what pim set.
So the code reads the tenant before every plan, rather than trusting what it applied last time.
And one choice of the kit's own: activations aren't standing state, so the read leaves them out.

7: The plan has a fixed order: groups, then policy rules, then grants, then removals.
And seven guards refuse a plan before anything is sent.
G one, a Tier 0 or Tier 1 policy losing approval or its approvers.
G two, a rule that allows permanent grants, or a grant with no end.
G three, a group set as its own approver.
G five, a group as a holder, or an eligible service principal.
And G seven, a self-service action in the plan.
One more choice: the pipeline's app doesn't create the P R V groups.
Microsoft Learn's reference for creating a group says a role-assignable group needs Role Management dot ReadWrite dot Directory.
The program keeps that permission off the pipeline, and a Privileged Role Administrator creates the groups by hand.
